class.name: CgameHydraulicErosion
class.brief_description: Deterministic droplet-based hydraulic erosion and thermal (talus) erosion of heightfields.
class.description: [CgameHydraulicErosion] is a native port of the GDScript [code]hydraulic_erosion.gd[/code] library. All methods are static: they take plain data and return a new array, and the input is never modified. Heights are stored row-major, indexed [code]y * width + x[/code]. [method erode] simulates water droplets that pick up sediment on slopes and deposit it where they slow down (Hans Beyer's particle model). Sediment is conserved: whatever a droplet picks up is deposited again, at the latest where it dies. For identical inputs and seed the result is identical, because the droplets use [RandomNumberGenerator] with the given seed. [method thermal] slides material down slopes steeper than a talus threshold. Each iteration is computed in two read-only passes over the heightfield, so large maps are processed on the [WorkerThreadPool] without changing the result. [codeblock] var eroded := CgameHydraulicErosion.erode(heights, 128, 128, 20000, 1234, {"capacity": 6.0}) eroded = CgameHydraulicErosion.thermal(eroded, 128, 128, 20, 0.6) [/codeblock]

method.name: erode
method.description: Returns an eroded copy of [param heights] after simulating [param droplets] droplets with the given [param seed]. Keys of [param params] override the values returned by [method get_default_params]. If [param width] or [param height] is smaller than 3, or the array size is not [code]width * height[/code], an unmodified copy is returned.

method.name: get_default_params
method.description: Returns the default erosion parameters: [code]inertia[/code] (0.05), [code]capacity[/code] (4.0), [code]deposition[/code] (0.3), [code]erosion[/code] (0.3), [code]evaporation[/code] (0.02), [code]gravity[/code] (4.0), [code]max_lifetime[/code] (30), [code]erosion_radius[/code] (2) and [code]min_slope[/code] (0.01).

method.name: max_slope
method.description: Returns the largest height difference between two 4-neighbouring cells. Useful to verify thermal erosion.

method.name: thermal
method.description: Returns a copy of [param heights] after [param iterations] passes of thermal erosion. Material moves to lower 4-neighbours where the drop exceeds [param talus] (height units per cell). Mass is conserved.
